text.p: Merrill Lynch on Thursday recommended investors accumulate loss-making Sahaviriya Steel Industry, saying it believed the firm would be able to turn losses into profit this year.
Merrill Lynch said in its report that SSI could make a net profit of 562 million baht ($21.7 million) or earnings per share of 1.1 baht this year after suffering heavy losses in 1995 and 1996.

Help from the government, rising demand for hot-rolled coil (HRC) which it produces and inadequate supply of local HRC were cited as factors that would lead to the turnaround of company's earnings this year.
The government recently imposed anti-dumping duties on steel products from Ukraine, Poland and Russia which it said dumped Thai market.
According to Merrill's forecast, SSI was likely to suffer a net loss of two billion baht for 1996 from 989 million in 1995.
The price of SSI shares now trading around 11.75 baht was also attractive, it said.
"The share price has fallen sharply by 83% since its high of 69.5 baht in February 1995," Merrill Lynch said.
"The stock is currently trading at 1997E (price/earning ratio) of 10.7...We believe that prospects are improving and the potential for share price appreciation is good," it said.
